title: Verification
text:
I follow you, with the nostalgia of centuries

that were not and will not be mine...

Not to have an unending age in which to love you!

To remain on your shore as on that of a young man

who runs toward his limits, my limited today.


I did not have nor will I have an eternity of you.

I am one minute of yours, and that hurts me so much

that I suffer in loving you, and would give you

more earth of myself, while keeping you in me.


Yes. I contemplate and hear you. I smell your seed

and, poor Sarah that I am, I do not return to you

what you come to give me.




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959
editorial_note: The translation preserves the limited minute of eternity and the Sarah allusion of unreturned fertility.

title: The Infinite
text:
You live in the dawn.

The birds acclaim you.

Joy dresses you in tunics of birds.

What dawn you exalt!

What noble light is yours!

Mornings and nights listen to you

because you are like a taper,

because you are like a roe deer.

To feel you passing,

brushing me with roses and ayes...

To ache on your knees, crushed

by crags and thickets.


And let a zephyr of larks come sweetly,

let you arrive, winnowing my wounds...

To be woman and yours, what ineffable

melting of consciousness in your arms!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dawn-lit beloved and the ecstatic melting of consciousness.

title: It Is a Day Celebrated in September...
text:
It is a day celebrated in September

each year.

Bowl of ruffs, offering of harvests from the sea.

At the rich man's table, invited

those who always ate his leavings.


The laden boats returned,

the longlines were more than enough this day.

The fish obtained without effort,

overflowed in waves!


To a few brief hours surrendered

a whole year of nights at the labor.


(Almost streaking dawn with invisible grays,

we went out to cast.

And the sudden cold east wind

forced us to set sail!)




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959
editorial_note: The translation keeps the September fishing feast and the cold levante forcing departure.

title: Naked and Adhered to Your Nakedness...
text:
Naked and adhered to your nakedness.

My breasts like freshly cut ice

on the flat water of your chest.

My shoulders opened beneath your shoulders.

And you, floating in my nakedness.


I will raise my arms and hold up your air.

You will be able to loosen my dream

because the sky will rest on my forehead.

Tributaries of your rivers will be my rivers.

We will sail together, you will be my sail,

and I will carry you through hidden seas.


What supreme effusion of geographies!

Your hands over my hands.

Your eyes, birds of my tree,

in the grass of my head.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the erotic geography of shared rivers, sail, and hidden seas.

title: They, Always Three, Are Your Coastal Angels...
text:
They, always three, are your coastal angels.

The three great mills that fly you,

snatch themselves with sun, turn drunk with blue,

salty sails

in the hands of the wind that bathes you.


Mills that in the field are ships

and here, now anchored sailboats, halo you.

How many boats in your village of waves,

the field spilling itself in white canvases!


Fresh water in the land of sowings,

water and sun at your farthest limits.

They turn and turn; oars, rigging,

without rudder—for you are it—over the skies.




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959
editorial_note: The translation keeps the three coastal windmills as angelic boats, sails, and rigging.

title: Days of East Wind
text:
The east wind admits no lords over you.

It alone lords over you!

Gray desert, or brown, your calm torso;

and the east wind

purring its love at you, with you.


I, yes. I, who float without moving,

inside the wind and your waters,

sleepily still, breathing you...

Solitude of light with clouds, high above.


Not a sail appears, nor a sweet oar

crackles, dripping you freshest water.

The east wind demands it, everyone flees

and gives you over to it, oh co-owning sea!


I am no longer the one I was; I come out covered

with tremendous eastern-wind solitudes.




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959
editorial_note: The translation keeps the levante as ruling east wind and the sea surrendered to it.

title: Grace
text:
The birds are going to sing. I feel it in my sides.

Because wings tremble in me that I never saw grow.

And suddenly the trees shake their messages

so I may gather them and carry them through the wind.


They will sprout stronger. I hear the earth

slide its warm moistures under my soles;

and a stream is not born unless a woman wants

it to gird her legs with its thin cloth.


I know gardens are coming. I know steeds leap.

Learning all that has cost me my life.

And I leave it to you in the marble, in case someone should find it

and want to know how so much is forgotten.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the bodily signs of birds, streams, and the life left in marble.

title: Dominion
text:
I need to have the soul tame

like a sad mastered beast,

to please it with barbs, the smoothness

of its skin dazzled in meekness.


It is necessary to tame it, so that its fever

not tremble in my blood for even a minute.

Let the fires of the thickest

oil of horror flood it, and let it resist.


Oh, my soft and subjected soul,

sweet beast enclosing itself in my body!

Lightning, screams, chill, and even people

urging it to come out. And it, dark.


I ask you, love, to allow me

to finish off my imprisoned tiger.

To give you (and free myself from this fury)

a still, unfading fragrance.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the soul as tamed beast and imprisoned tiger turned toward fragrance.

title: In No Man's Land
text:
In no man's land, on the dust

trodden by those who go and those who come,

I have pitched my tent without shelter

and I watch whether they go or return.

Some say I am among those who go,

although I am resting from the road.

Others "know" that I return, although I keep silent;

and my truest route I do not tell.

I tried to prove that where I am going

is to myself, only to myself, to have myself.

And they smile on hearing it, because all of them

are people who go, but who return.

Listen to me once: I no longer care

about the roads here, worth so much.

Because I walked once, I have already stopped

to root myself in the land that is no one's.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the road paradox and the decision to root in no one's land.

title: A Thousand Years Before You Are Like a Dream...
text:
A thousand years before You are like a dream.

Like the thickness of an avenue of waters.

Grass that grows in the morning,

blooms and grows in the morning

though by evening it is cut and dries.


What is time before You, what are the thunders

you brandish against me when you name me?

I feel terror at your idea, I see you grim

looking at me in the flame of your Archangel.

You are the sword too, the edge

and the pommel gripped by the fist.


To see Yourself you have born me.

So as not to be alone with your omnipotence.

I am nothingness, I am of time, I am a dream...

Water that flows to you, acid grass

that you cut without love...

You do not love me.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the psalm-like time image and the stark accusation that God does not love the speaker.
